newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks close mixed in busy trading.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks close mixed in busy trading.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended mixed and virtually flat on Tuesday after a busy session, bouncing back from Monday's slight loss as some issues stabilized after recent strong moves.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index added 5.63 points to close at 6473.04.
Turnover was heavy at 114.5 million shares worth C$1.7 billion ($1.2 billion).
"Bit of a rebound," said Dunnery Best, Midland Walwyn's director of private client investing. "It wasn't much of a day."
Declining stocks edged advancers 490 to 456, while 337 issues closed steady.
The index on Monday shed 25 points to close at 6467.
Nine of Toronto's 14 sub-groups ended higher, led by media, conglomerates, base metals and consumer products. The five weaker ones included influential oils and industrial products.
Toronto lagged New York, which broke the watershed 7500 point level. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 61 points to 7539 as international investors scouted for shares of blue- chip companies.
Among individual issues, Abacan Resource Corp. recovered slightly from Monday's nose-dive, adding 0.43 to 3.50 after losing 62 percent of its value.
The Calgary, Alberta-based oil firm, which topped Toronto actives, said on Monday that cash flows in 1997 and 1998 would be much lower than analysts' forecasts.

Class B shares of cable companies Rogers Communications Inc. and Shaw Communications Inc. rose on Monday's news that software giant Microsoft Corp. agreed to invest $1 billion in U.S. cable operator Comcast Corp.
Rogers jumped 0.95 to 9.20, while Shaw rose 0.35 to 10.
Takeover target Domco Inc. lost 1.50 to 18.50 in light trading after climbing 5.25 to 20 on Monday.

U.S. suitor Armstrong World Industries Inc. said it was disappointed after Domco's major shareholder, France's Sommer Allibert SA, declined to tender its 69 percent stake for the floor and wall-coverings firm.
But Armstrong said it would proceed with its C$488 million ($352 million) bid.
